name: Decoupled Appearance Modeling
definition: A method to handle appearance variations (e.g., uneven illumination) by producing a transformation map to adjust rendered images, preventing floaters caused by 3DGS trying to compensate for photometric changes.
summary: Decoupled Appearance Modeling is a post-processing CNN that generates per-pixel transformation maps to adjust rendered images for lighting variations, preventing 3D Gaussian Splatting from creating spurious geometry.
